name: VICI Properties
description: VICI Properties owns the real estate under 93 experiential assets in the U.S. and Canada (54 gaming properties and 39 other experiential properties, all 100 percent leased at Dec 31, 2025), including Caesars Palace, MGM Grand and the Venetian on the Las Vegas Strip, land on and near the Strip and four golf courses. It does not operate casinos: tenants such as Caesars, MGM and PENN sign long-term triple-net master leases, paying rent (usually with annual escalators) and covering taxes, insurance and maintenance. It also lends to operators and other experiential owners (three real estate debt investments with $966.0M of commitments in 2025). It has 28 employees. Las Vegas Strip properties produced about 49 percent of FY2025 revenue, and MGM and Caesars each accounted for about 36 to 37 percent of contractual rent.

gics.note: Conventional label recorded from general knowledge of the standard scheme; not re-checked against an MSCI/S&P source in this pass. SEC SIC code is 6798 (Real Estate Investment Trusts). The box misleads on the accounting: most VICI leases are accounted as sales-type leases or financing receivables, so revenue is booked as interest-like income on a long-term receivable rather than as rent, there is no depreciation on those assets, and net income ($2.8B) was 69 percent of revenue ($4.0B), far above a normal landlord. Economically the company is a lender-landlord to casino operators with 28 employees, and about half its revenue is tied to two tenants (MGM and Caesars) and to the Las Vegas Strip.

businessLines.name: Income from sales-type leases
businessLines.how: Tenants (casino operators) pay contractual triple-net rent under long-term master leases, typically with fixed or CPI-linked annual escalators; the accounting turns that rent into income on a receivable, with the tenant covering property costs.
businessLines.description: Master leases accounted for as sales-type (or direct financing) leases, so the landlord records interest on a lease receivable rather than rental income.

businessLines.name: Income from lease financing receivables, loans and securities
businessLines.how: Interest-like income on leases treated as financings and on loans to operators and experiential owners (funded loan commitments of $883.4M in 2025), fixed rate mostly, with tenants covering property costs.
businessLines.description: Leases accounted as financing arrangements, plus real estate loans and securities (the debt-investment program).

businessLines.name: Other income and golf revenues
businessLines.how: Golf: green fees and related revenue at courses it owns and operates directly; other income is mainly cost reimbursement with matching expense.
businessLines.description: Other income of $77.5M (largely reimbursed costs; other expenses equal other income in the 10-Q) and golf revenues of $39.8M from four championship golf courses.
